writeup.headline: Meta rates Hold at 64, one point below Buy, as strong quality offsets a high valuation.
writeup.thesis: Meta scores 64, a Hold that sits 1 point below the Buy edge at 65, so confidence is Medium. The business side is strong: revenue is up 28.0% year on year with an 81.8% gross margin and a 38.1% operating margin, and the balance sheet scores 93 with net cash. Growth still scores 70, though it slowed by 5.1 pp from the previous quarter. The main drag is valuation at 29. In absolute terms the multiples are high, at 8.3x sales and 46.2x free cash flow, and the FCF yield is 3.0 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield. Against its own history the stock is labelled expensive: P/FCF is more expensive than at 60 of the last 61 month-ends, while P/S and EV/EBIT are near the middle of the last 61 month-ends. Trend (65) and news (59) are modestly positive. The shares are 5.2% below their 52-week high but 4.6 pp behind QQQ over the last 126 trading days.
key_risks: Heavy AI spending: FY26 capex is guided at $130-145B, and the capex early warning is AMBER at 6/18.
Free cash flow margin of 17.9% lags the operating margin, which keeps P/FCF at 46.2x.
Revenue growth slowed by 5.1 pp from the previous quarter.
The FTC's appeal to revive its antitrust case and the remaining youth-harm trials.
what_would_change: A 1-point rise in the score would move the rating to Buy, for example through better trend or news after the October 21 Q3 results.
A lower valuation or faster free cash flow growth would lift the 29 valuation score.
A sharp slowdown in growth or a capex warning escalating beyond AMBER could weigh on the score, though falling to Sell would take a 20-point drop below 45.
